To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) inequality, operationalized by the Gini Index, is significantly related to educational expectations, (ii) inequality is significantly related to occupational expectations, and (iii) inequality is positively related to both educational and occupational expectations after controlling for academic achievement, gender, family and school characteristics.

(i) students from more unequal societies expect more from themselves in terms of education and occupation and (ii) this is not explained by the level of academic achievement, family background, gender, school characteristics or the level of economic inequality.
inequality is positively associated with educational and occupational expectations among 15-year olds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the level of inequality in society is associated with higher expectations among students, and if so, what are the mechanisms that explain this phenomenon?
the relationship between inequality and the formation of expectations.
the relationship between social inequality and educational and occupational expectations, which we argue is a neglected area of research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inequality is not only a problem of social justice but also a problem of educational effectiveness.
the relationship between inequality and expectations is not straightforward, but that the effect is likely to be positive.
there is an association between inequality and life plans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more unequal the society, the more ambitious the students are.
“inequality is good for expectations but bad for performance”.
inequality is a double-edged sword.
The main takeaway from our work is that

inequality may have a negative effect on the educational and occupational aspirations of young people, and that this is likely to affect the educational and labour market outcomes of future generations of adults.
inequality may not only have negative effects on actual educational performance, it also may have negative effects on the formation of expectations.
we need to be careful in interpreting the meaning of expectations and that we should be aware that expectations may not always be a reliable predictor for actual performance.
